question: CI #226 tests/m5-replay.test.ts sniper exceeded its 180000 ms test timeout; is this a node-2 regression?
method: Read-only extraction of the npm test step of test-and-build-sample1 from GitHub Actions logs (full logs, no reruns). No timeout or threshold changed.
workload: Identical in every row from c109d4e on: cannon 194/8467, sniper 182/11930, mage 176/12380, sniper-caitlyn 185/11571 (commands/ticks).
findings: The node-2 base c109d4e fails the same way on identical work (run 224 attempt 1: sniper 184.45 s, timed out); its passing attempt left 1.9 s.
The same commit abd2ed8 measured 138.37 s (run 225) and 186.64 s (run 226): runner-to-runner spread of about 35% with no code difference.
Node-2 samples (138.37, 186.64, 175.63 s) lie within the base distribution (184.45, 178.12 s); no node-2 regression is shown, and none is excluded.
Vitest runs files in parallel (forks pool, no config); m6-integration overlaps the sniper replay in every sample, so the replay shares the runner CPU.
Sniper is the longest replay (182 commands, 11930 ticks, every command and tick restored), so it sits closest to the fixed 180 s timeout.
disposition: Kept as an independent, pre-existing performance issue: no CI rerun to get green, the 180 s timeout is not raised, and no test is skipped. A fix (making the replay check cheaper without weakening it, or isolating it from parallel files) needs its own decision.
